en: Delicious ends in -cious, like precious and gracious.
Which spelling is correct? (wanting to do well)
The root word “ambition” has a t, so we write -tious.
Which spelling is correct? (able to be seen)
“Vis” is not a full word on its own, so it takes -ible.
Which spelling is correct? (cosy and relaxing)
“Comfort” is a complete word, so we add -able.
Which spelling is correct? (to get something)
After c, the rule is e before i: receive.
Which spelling is correct? (to think something is true)
Here the sound is “ee” and there is no c, so i comes before e.
Which spelling is correct? (a soldier who wore armour long ago)
“Knight” has a silent k and a silent gh.
Which spelling is correct? (land with water all around it)
“Weird” breaks the i before e rule, so it has to be learned.
Necessary has one c and two s’s.
Which spelling is correct? (able to happen)
“Poss” is not a full word, so it takes -ible, and there are two s’s.
Which spelling is correct? (can be trusted)
From “rely”: the y changes to i and we add -able.
Which spelling is correct? (worth a lot and dearly loved)
Which spelling is correct? (good for your body)
Like “nutrition”, it has a t, so it ends in -tious.
Which spelling is correct? (the short, thick finger)
“Thumb” has a silent b at the end.
Which spelling is correct? (the top of a room)
After c, the rule is e before i: ceiling.
Which spelling is correct? (someone you like and trust)
“Friend” has i before e. Remember: a friend to the end.
Which spelling is correct? (the study of the world around us)
“Science” has a silent c after the s.
Which spelling is correct? (showing good sense)
Which spelling is correct? (very sweet and lovable)
From the word “adore”: drop the e and add -able.
Which spelling is correct? (the joint between your hand and arm)
Which spelling is correct? (awake and aware)
Conscious has “sc” in the middle and ends in -cious.
Which spelling is correct? (feeling that something is not right)
Like “suspicion”, it uses a c, so it ends in -cious.
Which spelling is correct? (careful to avoid danger)
Like “caution”, it has a t, so it ends in -tious.
Which spelling is correct? (from another country)
“Foreign” breaks the i before e rule and has a silent g.
Which spelling is correct? (a baby sheep)
Which spelling is correct? (a feeling of not being sure)
Which spelling is correct? (very nasty or unpleasant)
“Horr” is not a full word, so it takes -ible.
Which spelling is correct? (apart, not together)
Remember: there is “a rat” in sep-a-rate.
Which spelling is correct? (the beat in music)
“Rhythm” has a silent h after the r and no vowel between th and m.

en.title: Spelling rules
en.teach: Some spelling patterns help: -cious and -tious endings (delicious, ambitious), -able after a full word (comfortable), i before e except after c (receive), and silent letters (knight, thumb).
